text:
Gage Goncalves had a breakout last season by any measure. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.5 wins above replacement, 32nd among forwards, mostly from even-strength offense. This season, 19 games in, he has no goals.

That drought deserves a closer look before anyone worries. He has 2.6 expected goals, so he keeps getting the looks, and goals tend to follow chances. His team has also scored 4.6 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. The Lightning take 60.4% of the expected goals at five on five when he's out there, 4.5 points better than without him. That isn't a player losing his game.

There are two honest caveats. Evolving-Hockey also noted last season's results ran ahead of his chances (2.5 wins against 1.4 expected), so some regression was always coming. And his ice time has slipped by more than two minutes over the last 10 games, with three nights under 12. Our range still has him around eight goals, which tells you how much of this is the puck refusing to go in rather than anything he's doing wrong.
